title: Quantification of Fibrosis and Airspace Availability in Lung Using ImageJ/Fiji
author: Bertrand-David Ségard
materials: Air ducts and air ducts walls definition
Overlay of tissue and airspace segmentation

steps.title: Perform Sample Detection
steps.instruction: Detect the sample in the image using the Fibrosis script.

substeps.instruction: Open the image to be analyzed (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Sample detection).
Define the image scale (px / μm) and click OK.
Define the lower (strongly stained tissue) and upper (lightly stained tissue) thresholds; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Apply Automatic Particle Filter
steps.instruction: Filter particles from the sample mask automatically.

substeps.instruction: Open the mask obtained from the sample detection step (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Particle filter auto).
Define the minimal and maximal size cutoffs; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Perform Manual Background Cleaning
steps.instruction: Manually remove undesirable background objects from the mask.

substeps.instruction: Open the mask obtained from the automatic particle filter step (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Particle filter manual).
Use a selection tool (e.g., Rectangle) to select and delete undesirable background objects (do not clean particles in air ducts).
Check the 'Confirm cleaning' box and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Define Sample Border
steps.instruction: Establish the border of the sample.

substeps.instruction: Open the cleaned mask (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Border definition).
Use a drawing tool (e.g., Pencil Tool) to repair breaks in the sample border; check 'Confirm correction' and click OK.
Define the size of the border; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Identify Air Ducts
steps.instruction: Manually identify and select air ducts within the sample.

substeps.instruction: Open the cleaned mask (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Air duct identification).
Check the 'Add new air duct' box and click OK to enter selection mode.
Use a selection tool (e.g., Wand (tracing) tool) to select air ducts one by one, clicking OK to validate each selection.
Check the 'Confirm selection' box and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Define Air Duct Walls
steps.instruction: Define the walls of the identified air ducts.

substeps.instruction: Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Air ducts walls definition).
Define the size of air ducts walls; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Extract Parenchyma
steps.instruction: Extract the parenchyma using the original image and generated masks/ROIs.

substeps.instruction: Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Parenchyma extraction).
When prompted, open the following files: original sample image, clean mask, sample border ROI set, and air ducts walls ROI set.
Define the image scale (px / μm) and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Pre-process MT Stained Samples
steps.instruction: Perform pre-processing for Masson's Trichrome (MT) stained parenchyma images using Fiji (required for Colour Deconvolution plugin).

substeps.instruction: Open the parenchyma image (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > MT pre-processing).
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Detect Fibrosis
steps.instruction: Detect fibrotic tissue in the parenchyma.

substeps.instruction: Open the parenchyma image (for SR) or the connective tissue in the parenchyma (for MT) (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Fibrosis detection).
Define the image scale (px / μm) and click OK.
Define the lower and upper thresholds; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Visualize Tissue
steps.instruction: Generate a visualization of the tissue regions of interest.

substeps.instruction: Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Visualization tissue).
When prompted, open: original sample image, parenchyma ROI set, sample border ROI set, air ducts walls ROI set, air ducts ROI set, and fibrosis ROI set.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Detect Airspace
steps.instruction: Quantify and detect airspace within the parenchyma.

substeps.instruction: Open the parenchyma image, sample border ROI set, and air ducts walls ROI set when prompted.
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Airspace detection).
Define the minimal and maximal size and circularity cutoffs; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Filter Fibrosis
steps.instruction: Clean the fibrosis mask using automatic size filters.

substeps.instruction: Open the fibrotic tissue mask (File > Open…).
Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Fibrosis filter auto).
Define the minimal and maximal size cutoffs; check 'Confirm settings' and click OK.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Visualize Tissue and Airspace
steps.instruction: Create a final combined visualization of tissue and airspace.

substeps.instruction: Launch the script (Plugins > Fibrosis > Visualization tissue airspace).
When prompted, open the tissue visualization image and the airspace ROI set.
Check the 'Save' box, select the desired folder, and click OK.

steps.title: Compile Results
steps.instruction: Calculate fibrosis and airspace ratios using the exported CSV data.

substeps.instruction: Extract Parenchyma area from Results.csv.
Extract Fibrosis area from Summary.csv (Total Area).
Extract Airspace area from Summary.csv (Total Area).
Calculate Ratio fibrosis/parenchyma = Fibrosis area / Parenchyma area.
Calculate Ratio airspace/sample = Airspace area / (Parenchyma area + Airspace area).
